stories.research_notes:
Here is a research note on the event, based on available sources.

---

## Event Summary

- *What was done*: Code of Nature, a South Korean ecological restoration company, applied a moss-based soil restoration treatment (their product “Mosby”) by drone to a wildfire‐burned site in Gyeongpo district, Gangneung City, Gangwon Province, South Korea. ([streetinsider.com](https://www.streetinsider.com/Business%2BWire/Code%2Bof%2BNatures%2BMoss-Based%2BSolution%2BSpeeds%2BSoil%2BRecovery%2Bat%2BSouth%2BKorean%2BWildfire%2BSite/27399391.html?utm_source=openai))  
- *When*: The wildfire burned part of the site in 2023; the treatment was carried out in August 2024. Soil was sampled 13 months later, around September 2025. ([streetinsider.com](https://www.streetinsider.com/Business%2BWire/Code%2Bof%2BNatures%2BMoss-Based%2BSolution%2BSpeeds%2BSoil%2BRecovery%2Bat%2BSouth%2BKorean%2BWildfire%2BSite/27399391.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Measured Outcomes

From sampling undertaken 13 months post-treatment:

- Soil organic matter rose from **0.21% to 1.85%**, i.e. nearly ninefold. ([streetinsider.com](https://www.streetinsider.com/Business%2BWire/Code%2Bof%2BNatures%2BMoss-Based%2BSolution%2BSpeeds%2BSoil%2BRecovery%2Bat%2BSouth%2BKorean%2BWildfire%2BSite/27399391.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Total nitrogen (T-N) increased from **0.008% to 0.063%**. ([streetinsider.com](https://www.streetinsider.com/Business%2BWire/Code%2Bof%2BNatures%2BMoss-Based%2BSolution%2BSpeeds%2BSoil%2BRecovery%2Bat%2BSouth%2BKorean%2BWildfire%2BSite/27399391.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Available phosphate tripled: from **10.65 mg/kg to 33.4 mg/kg**. ([streetinsider.com](https://www.streetinsider.com/Business%2BWire/Code%2Bof%2BNatures%2BMoss-Based%2BSolution%2BSpeeds%2BSoil%2BRecovery%2Bat%2BSouth%2BKorean%2BWildfire%2BSite/27399391.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Over the first three months after application, microbial activity averaged **1.8×** the level before restoration. ([streetinsider.com](https://www.streetinsider.com/Business%2BWire/Code%2Bof%2BNatures%2BMoss-Based%2BSolution%2BSpeeds%2BSoil%2BRecovery%2Bat%2BSouth%2BKorean%2BWildfire%2BSite/27399391.html?utm_source=openai))  

Other reported outcomes as part of the Gyeongpo project (from Code of Nature’s site) include:

- More than **50% ground cover** achieved (i.e. moss and other vegetative/stabilizing cover) over the treated area. ([c-of-n.com](https://www.c-of-n.com/en/mosby/projects/gyeongpo-wildfire?utm_source=openai))  
- NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) improved by more than **20%**. ([c-of-n.com](https://www.c-of-n.com/en/mosby/projects/gyeongpo-wildfire?utm_source=openai))  
- Soil physicochemical properties improved by more than **20%**. ([c-of-n.com](https://www.c-of-n.com/en/mosby/projects/gyeongpo-wildfire?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Source Origin

- The detailed data (organic matter, nutrients, microbial activity) come from a **press release** by Code of Nature, distributed via Business Wire and published November 25, 2026. ([streetinsider.com](https://www.streetinsider.com/Business%2BWire/Code%2Bof%2BNatures%2BMoss-Based%2BSolution%2BSpeeds%2BSoil%2BRecovery%2Bat%2BSouth%2BKorean%2BWildfire%2BSite/27399391.html?utm_source=openai))  
- On Code of Nature’s own website (“Gangneung Gyeongpo Wildfire Soil Restoration Project” page) similar claims are made, including the same figures. ([c-of-n.com](https://www.c-of-n.com/en/mosby/projects/gyeongpo-wildfire?utm_source=openai))  
- A Korean media report (“산불 복원 이야기 4”) published September 29, 2026 summarizes those numbers, citing the “2025 강릉 경포 산불피해지 토양 복원사업 결과 보고서 (Code of Nature, December 2025)”. ([itaseoul.org](https://itaseoul.org/content/602a8e4c-bbc3-4a47-9416-31202ff38fe4?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Independent Verification / Caveats

No peer‐reviewed scientific article or an independent academic source was found at the time of this search that verifies the results *after the full field application* at the Gyeongpo wildfire site under controlled or published study conditions.

- There is an academic paper from *Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology* by Code of Nature and collaborators (Jang, Kang, Park, et al.) on moss inoculation in reclaimed coastal lands (Taean, South Korea) showing that moss application under controlled pot experiments increases soil organic matter, available phosphate, CEC, etc. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42449066/?utm_source=openai))  
- That study is a *proof of concept in container/pot trials* and *not the same site*, and does *not include long-term field trials or wildfire sites* of the same type. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42449066/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Assessment: What Actually Happened

- These are **measured outcomes** rather than just a pledge or announcement: the numbers reported for soil organic matter, nitrogen, phosphate, ground cover, microbial activity, and NDVI are from actual soil and vegetation monitoring following treatment.  
- The results appear to come entirely from the implementing organization (Code of Nature) and the accompanying project report; there is no independently published scientific study (as of yet) that validates specifically these field findings at Gyeongpo.  
- The source is consistent: the same figures are used in multiple places, but all trace back to Code of Nature’s materials (press release, project report, and company communications).  

---

## Remaining Uncertainties

- Whether sampling and measurement followed standard scientific protocols (controls, replicates, blind sampling, independent auditing) is not clearly documented in accessible sources.  
- Longevity of effects beyond 13 months (e.g. whether organic matter continues to increase, whether plant species beyond moss and early vegetation regenerate) is not yet reported.  
- Independent validation or peer review of the Gyeongpo project field results would strengthen confidence.  

---

## Conclusion

What we *do* know:

- Code of Nature applied a moss-based soil treatment (“Mosby”) to a 2023 wildfire site in Gyeongpo, Gangneung.  
- Within 13 months, they report large improvements in soil organic matter (from 0.21% → 1.85%), total nitrogen, available phosphate (tripled), microbial activity, NDVI, ground cover.  

What we *don’t yet have*:

- Independent academic confirmation of those field results for Gyeongpo.  
- Full methodological detail from an external party to confirm rigor.  

---

If you like, I can try to locate whether there is an upcoming peer-reviewed paper or third-party verification of these results, or compare with other moss-based restoration field trials globally.

stories.research_notes:
Here is what the available sources say about the claim in the headline “South African superantibodies advance HIV vaccine development” and what is *actually* established so far. I found no evidence of a single scientific paper matching *exactly* the headline’s details; many news sources are drawing on a recent *feature* in *Nature* that synthesizes multiple recent studies rather than a newly completed trial. Below is a factual breakdown, distinguishing observed outcomes from plans or early-stage work.

---

## What *does* exist: Key sources

**Primary source / scientific studies:**

1. **“Early immune responses linked to protective HIV antibodies”**  
   - A study published in *PLoS Pathogens* in April 2026, by South African and international scientists. ([wits.ac.za](https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/research-news/2026/2026-03/early-immune-responses-linked-to-protective-hiv-antibodies-.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - It analyzed **42 blood samples** from **14 recently HIV-infected persons** in South Africa, followed over time. ([wits.ac.za](https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/research-news/2026/2026-03/early-immune-responses-linked-to-protective-hiv-antibodies-.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - The work found that those who later developed *broadly neutralizing antibodies* (bnAbs) had distinct immune activation patterns early in infection. ([wits.ac.za](https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/research-news/2026/2026-03/early-immune-responses-linked-to-protective-hiv-antibodies-.html?utm_source=openai))  

2. **“B cell repertoire analysis … in southern African population”**  
   - Study published November 2026 (Frontiers in Immunology) with young HIV-negative South African women (age 18-23), some of whom later acquired HIV. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1995891/abstract?utm_source=openai))  
   - It mapped the prevalence of antibody-gene features associated with bnAb precursors, showing that these precursors exist in the naïve IgM B cell pool long before infection or treatment. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1995891/abstract?utm_source=openai))  

3. **“Genetic divergence … does not confer consistent compartment-specific differences in broadly neutralizing antibody sensitivity”**  
   - From *Journal of Virology*, published September 2026. ([journals.asm.org](https://journals.asm.org/doi/epdf/10.1128/jvi.01151-26?utm_source=openai))  
   - Compared HIV envelope (Env) variants from different tissue compartments (blood, lymph nodes) in individuals on antiretroviral therapy (ART), and tested their sensitivity to bnAbs.  
   - Key finding: Although genetic differences exist between compartments, *most bnAbs tested* retained broadly similar ability to neutralize variants across compartments. Particularly, antibodies targeting the CD4-binding site and the gp120-gp41 interface remained effective across tissues. ([journals.asm.org](https://journals.asm.org/doi/epdf/10.1128/jvi.01151-26?utm_source=openai))  

**Secondary / journalistic source:**

- Ewen Callaway’s *Nature* feature (“A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies”, 25 Nov 2026) describes these and other recent advances. It highlights the story of CAP256, a South African donor whose antibody response to HIV (in the mid-2000s) has served as a key model for vaccine research. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03718-4?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What *is claimed or proposed*, but *not yet measured*

These are outcomes or goals described in the news story, which are not yet established:

- The headline suggests that “superantibodies” (i.e. very potent bnAbs) discovered in one South African patient (CAP256) are driving a major advance toward a vaccine. In fact, CAP256 indeed developed exceptionally broad and potent bnAbs naturally years ago; but the vaccine strategy inspired by her has not yet produced in humans bnAbs at the full potency and breadth achieved naturally. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03718-4?utm_source=openai))  
- Several vaccine candidates or immunogens (including those engineered in labs, such as “eOD-GT8”, and immunogens derived from CAP256 virus strains) are currently in **preclinical** or **very early human trial** phases. Some have shown promising results in primates; others have succeeded in activating *precursors* of bnAbs in human volunteers. But none have yet demonstrated full bnAb generation in humans sufficient to prevent HIV infection. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03718-4?utm_source=openai))  
- The news reports state that in monkeys a vaccination strategy has *triggered the production* of broadly neutralizing antibodies — that seems accurate: there are preclinical (animal) experiments that show success. Yet this is not the same as a human trial showing protection. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03718-4?utm_source=openai))

---

## What is *measured out*

The concrete, measured outcomes so far include:

- Identification in several South African HIV-infected individuals of immune signatures (very early immune activation, particular B cell repertoire features) that correlate with eventual development of bnAbs. ([wits.ac.za](https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/research-news/2026/2026-03/early-immune-responses-linked-to-protective-hiv-antibodies-.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Demonstration that key bnAbs maintain neutralization potency across different tissue compartments even during ART, despite genetic variation in HIV Env sequences. ([journals.asm.org](https://journals.asm.org/doi/epdf/10.1128/jvi.01151-26?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Conclusion: What is real vs. what’s still in progress

- **Real, measured progress**: Research has confirmed that some HIV-infected people (like CAP256) naturally develop highly potent and broad bnAbs; that these antibody precursors are present in naïve B cell repertoires in South African populations; that genetic variation between viral reservoirs does *not* abolish bnAb sensitivity for certain antibody classes. These are empirical, published findings.  

- **Still unverified/planned**: No human vaccine yet has been shown to produce such bnAbs at the level needed to prevent HIV infection. Vaccine/immunogen strategies (germline targeting, immunogens derived from CAP256, eOD-GT8 etc.) have shown promise in animal models or in activating precursor cells in humans, but full protective efficacy in human trials is not yet demonstrated.

---

If you like, I can try to find the *exact* Nature article(s) underlying the feature to see if any results beyond precursors have been published, so you have full clarity.

### Research note

- **Outcome:** The rescue was completed, not merely announced as a plan. Colombian police and military entered the Éxito supermarket in Cartagena in the early hours of **November 25, 2026**. President Abelardo de la Espriella and police said all those held were freed; police’s statement, quoted by local outlet *El Universal*, said they were safe. ([abcnews.com](https://abcnews.com/amp/International/30-hostages-rescued-after-standoff-colombia-president-officials/story?id=138436242))
- **Hostage count is uncertain:** The president initially estimated **about 30** people were held. AP later reported the army said **more than 50** had been held, while *The Guardian* reported police’s final figure was **about 70**. Ten people had reportedly been released before the final operation. So “about 30 rescued” is not a well-supported final count; “all hostages rescued” is the better-supported outcome. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/colombia-supermarket-exito-cartagena-hostages-c6b9c0ca799ff611148fc87d4b323628))
- **Other reported details:** Authorities said one man was killed. The number of people detained varies across reports; *The Guardian* reported four arrests. It also noted questions about whether the man killed was in fact a hostage, so that detail is not fully settled in the reporting. ([abcnews.com](https://abcnews.com/amp/International/30-hostages-rescued-after-standoff-colombia-president-officials/story?id=138436242))
- **Sources and independence:** The Colombian presidency’s published statement on November 24 confirms the hostage crisis and response, but predates the rescue. The direct police X post announcing the rescue is reproduced in *El Universal*’s report; X itself blocked access during this search. AP and *The Guardian* provide independent reporting. CBS identifies its report as CBS/AFP, so it is agency-based rather than a separate primary account. ([presidencia.gov.co](https://www.presidencia.gov.co/prensa/Paginas/Comunicado-Gobierno-Nacional-despliega-capacidades-especiales-de-la-Fuerza-Publica-para-liberar-a-personas-20261124.aspx?utm_source=openai))

stories.research_notes:
Aqui está um panorama confirmado sobre o evento “Prefeitura inicia obras para restauração dos lagos da Praça da República”, baseado em fontes primárias e independentes:

---

## O que realmente aconteceu

- A Prefeitura de São Paulo deu início a obras de **recuperação estrutural, impermeabilização e restauro dos lagos da Praça da República**. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  
- Os sistemas hidráulico e elétrico também serão modernizados: haverá substituição de tubulação antiga e instalação de dois novos conjuntos motor-bomba e filtros de alta capacidade. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  
- Também constam da obra: instalação de filtros nos vertedouros para reter folhas e plástico, sistema de aeração no fundo dos lagos para evitar acúmulo de sujeira, recuperação de elementos decorativos e arquitetônicos (chafarizes, pontilhões, guarda-corpos de ferro, pilaretes ornamentais, pedras artificiais dos lagos) e repintura do fundo dos lagos no tom verde original do projeto histórico. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Detalhes sobre investimento, cronograma e execução

- Valor da intervenção: **R$ 3.925.579,38**; estimativa inicial de licitação indicava R$ 4.046.987,80, mas o valor homologado foi o primeiro. ([achaedital.com.br](https://achaedital.com.br/licitacao/sp-secretaria-municipal-das-subprefeituras-49269236000117-1-000025-2026?utm_source=openai))  
- Órgão responsável: Secretaria Municipal das Subprefeituras (SMSUB), Prefeitura de São Paulo. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  
- Duração prevista: **10 meses** a partir do início das obras. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  

---

## O que era plano vs. o que foi iniciado (comprovação de execução)

- As medidas descritas estão em andamento — já foram iniciadas obras de engenharia, com isolamento ao redor dos lagos, etc. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  
- Essa não é apenas uma promessa ou plano: é uma obra iniciada efetivamente. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Motivo e contexto

- Problemas anteriores detectados incluem infiltrações, vazamentos entre 2024 e 2025, e aumento no consumo de água dos lagos devido a isso. Os lagos não passaram por reforma completa dos sistemas hidráulico e elétrico desde 2007. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  
- A Praça da República é uma área tombada; por isso, o projeto de restauro obriga critérios rigorosos para preservar estética e elementos arquitetônicos históricos. ([prefeitura.sp.gov.br](https://prefeitura.sp.gov.br/web/subprefeituras/w/prefeitura-de-sao-paulo-inicia-obras-de-recuperacao-e-restauro-dos-lagos-da-praca-da-republica?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Limitações ou ausências de confirmação

- Até agora não há informação divulgada sobre qual empresa foi contratada, nem detalhes sobre medições iniciais de vazamento ou perda de água quantificadas em litros ou porcentagem.  
- Também não há confirmação pública de quando exatamente as obras começaram (dia/mês), apenas que muitas medidas já estão sendo executadas.  
- Não há dados sobre monitoramento ambiental, como fauna aquática após as obras, que confirmem impactos positivos concretos — por exemplo, retorno da população de peixes ou redução medida de consumo de água.

---

Se quiser, posso checar imagens recentes ou relatórios técnicos para confirmar o estado atual dos lagos, ou estimativas sobre economia de água ou melhoria da qualidade da água após a obra. Deseja que prossiga nessa direção?

### Research note

- **What happened:** Mato Grosso’s environment secretariat (Sema-MT) reported on **November 23, 2026** that the state government, the PCI Institute and Mercuria Energy Group had signed a partnership at COP 31. The stated plan is for Mercuria to provide **R$100 million** toward restoring **up to 15,000 hectares** in the Vale do Juruena, Alto Teles Pires and Tangará da Serra regions. The announcement also describes a separate **R$612,000** payment to PCI for producer outreach and work on carbon-credit mechanisms. ([secom.mt.gov.br](https://www.secom.mt.gov.br/w/governo-de-mt-garante-parceria-de-r-100-milh%C3%B5es-para-recupera%C3%A7%C3%A3o-de-%C3%A1reas-degradadas))

- **Status:** This is an **agreement and planned investment**, not evidence that restoration has been completed. The announcement gives no project start date, disbursement schedule or measured hectares restored. It separately says LEAF Coalition investors expressed interest in buying future credits; that is not a completed credit sale. ([secom.mt.gov.br](https://www.secom.mt.gov.br/w/governo-de-mt-garante-parceria-de-r-100-milh%C3%B5es-para-recupera%C3%A7%C3%A3o-de-%C3%A1reas-degradadas))

- **Source check:** The primary source is Sema-MT’s announcement. HiperNotícias also reported the agreement, but its account substantially tracks the same announced terms; a G1 report is available through a republication that identifies G1 as the byline and Sema-MT as its source for the agreement. These reports do not independently verify funding or restoration results. ([hnt.com.br](https://www.hnt.com.br/cidades/governo-fecha-parceria-de-r-100-milhoes-para-recuperar-ate-15-mil-hectares-degradados/588511))

- **Date note:** The candidate is dated **November 25**, but the state’s original announcement was published **November 23, 2026**.

stories.research_notes:
I looked for credible sources to verify the candidate story: “Patient recovery story highlights importance of blood donation” (Brazil / Volta Redonda / patient with severe thrombocytopenia “plaquetopenia grave”).

---
